title: 第71章 谷中风云第72章 秦川的名声

> 第71章 谷中风云（第1页）
苏木槿将秦川的建议——公开学术报告——转达给薛忘忧，是在第二天上午。
当天傍晚，薛忘忧在药庐的小书房里召见了秦川。这次没有苏木槿陪同，只有两人对坐。薛忘忧面前的桌上摊着一本翻开的医案，写着密密麻麻的批注，批注的字迹很小，每一笔都工整如印刷。秦川注意到那本医案的书脊上贴着一张泛黄的标签，标签上的字是手写的：《凡人医案辑录·卷一》。这让他心里微微一动——谷主本人，也一直在做凡人医疗的研究。
“木槿跟我说了你的想法。公开报告，所有弟子都可旁听，讲凡人医疗的研究进展。”薛忘忧开门见山，“这个想法很好。但需要选对时机。你的研究才刚开始——能讲的内容够不够一次报告？”
“够。”秦川说，“我不是讲成果，是讲思路。凡人医疗不是一个新领域，是百草谷一直存在但没有系统化的空白。我只需要把这十几天研究的东西梳理出来，告诉弟子们这个领域的存在和可能性就够了。”
薛忘忧沉默了片刻，将手中的笔搁在笔山上。“百草谷向来标榜以医道济世，但实际上，我们只济了一半——修士那一半。凡人这一半，不是不想济，是体系不对。你能帮我们补上这一半，是谷中欠你的人情。但人情归人情，规矩归规矩。丹堂长老沈鹤眠今天下午找过我。他说你一个凡人，没有经过百草谷正规考核，在藏书阁翻阅医典也就罢了，还要在弟子面前做报告——不合规矩。”
“我问他，什么规矩。他说百草谷第七十二条谷规：凡外聘人员需经堂口考核方可执教。我说秦川没有执教，他只是做一场交流报告，不占编制，不参与考核，不给学分。”薛忘忧顿了顿，缓缓说道，“沈鹤眠说那也不行，坏了风气。我说——他要是能让中界八成凡人看上病，这个风气，坏就坏了。”
秦川沉默了一瞬，微微颔首。薛忘忧敢在长老面前这么力挺他，显然不仅仅是因为钱不缺那封信——更是因为秦川的思路触动了他多年未解决的盲区：百草谷有最好的药材和医典，却始终无法惠及中界人口八成的凡人。
“不用谢。”薛忘忧拿起笔，继续写批注，“我不是帮你。我是帮那些我们亏欠了很久的人。”他顿了顿，“报告时间定在五天后。地点在中堂大讲堂。我会让木槿协助你准备——届时各堂都会有人来。不只是弟子，长老们也会来旁听。”
秦川站起身，告辞离开。走出药庐时，他在石板桥上停了一下。溪水在脚下流过，泛着淡蓝色的光。他忽然有一种很奇怪的感受——在地球上，他做过无数次产品发布会的演讲，但那些演讲的服务对象是用户和投资人。这一次，他的演讲对象是一群修行了百年千年的修士，他要向他们解释一个他们从未正眼看过的领域：凡人的身体。
这大概是他做过的最难的演讲。也是最有意义的一场。
他沿着石板路走回竹楼，推开门的动作不急不缓。桌上已经摊开了他之前整理的资料——孙老六的病例记录、李神医的医案批注、沈青黛整理的禁忌药材名录、还有他自己密密麻麻写了小半本的笔记。他坐下来，开始拟演讲提纲。
第一页，他写下了报告题目：《凡人医药基础之观察与思辨》。

> Chapter 71 Wind and Cloud in the Valley (Page 1)
Su Mujin conveyed Qin Chuan's suggestion—disclosure of academic reports—to Xue Wangyou the next morning.
In the evening of that day, Xue Wangyou summoned Qin Chuan in the small study room of Yaolu. This time there was no Su Muxin accompanying him, only two people sitting opposite each other. There was an open medical record spread out on the table in front of Xue Wangyou, with dense notes written in them. The handwriting of the notes was very small, and every stroke was as neat as printing. Qin Chuan noticed that there was a yellowed label on the spine of the medical record. The words on the label were handwritten: "Mortal Medical Records Volume 1". This made him feel a little moved - the Valley Master himself has been doing research on mortal medical treatment.
"Mujin told me your idea. It will be a public report that all disciples can listen to, and talk about the research progress of mortal medical treatment." Xue Wangyou got straight to the point, "This is a good idea. But you need to choose the right time. Your research has just begun - is the content you can talk about enough for one report?"
"Enough." Qin Chuan said, "I'm not talking about results, but ideas. Mortal medicine is not a new field, it is a gap that has always existed in Baicao Valley but has not been systematized. I just need to sort out what I have studied in the past ten days and tell the disciples about the existence and possibility of this field."
Xue Wangyou was silent for a moment and placed the pen in his hand on the mountain of pens. "Baicao Valley has always boasted of using medicine to help the world, but in fact, we only helped half - the half of the monks. The mortal half is not because we don't want to help, but because the system is wrong. You can help us make up for this half, which is a favor that the valley owes you. But the favor It’s a matter of human nature and rules. The elder of the Dan Hall, Shen Hemian, came to see me this afternoon. He said that you are a mortal who has not gone through the formal assessment of Baicao Valley. You only read the medical books in the library, and you have to give a report in front of the disciples - it is against the rules. "
"I asked him what the rules were. He said the 72nd rule of Baicao Valley: All external staff must pass the entrance examination before they can teach. I said Qin Chuan did not teach, he just gave an exchange report, did not occupy the staff, did not participate in the assessment, and did not give credits."
Qin Chuan was silent for a moment and nodded slightly. The reason why Xue Wangyou dared to support him so much in front of the elders was obviously not only because of the letter about the lack of money - but also because Qin Chuan's thinking touched a blind spot that he had not solved for many years: Baicao Valley has the best medicinal materials and medical classics, but it has never been able to benefit 80% of the mortals in the middle world.
"You're welcome." Xue Wangyou picked up the pen and continued to write notes, "I'm not helping you. I'm helping those who we have owed money to for a long time." He paused, "The report time is set for five days. The location will be in the main lecture hall. I will let Mu Jin help you prepare - there will be people from each hall by then. Not only the disciples, the elders will also come to listen."
Qin Chuan stood up, said goodbye and left. When he walked out of the medicine house, he stopped for a moment on the stone bridge. The stream flows under the feet, glowing with light blue. He suddenly had a very strange feeling - on earth, he had given countless speeches at product launches, but those speeches were aimed at users and investors. This time, he was speaking to a group of monks who had been practicing for hundreds of thousands of years. He wanted to explain to them a field they had never seen directly: the mortal body.
This was probably the most difficult speech he had ever given. It is also the most meaningful one.
He walked back to the bamboo house along the stone road and opened the door slowly and slowly. The information he had compiled before was already spread out on the table - Sun Laoliu's case records, Dr. Li's medical notes, the list of taboo medicinal materials compiled by Shen Qingdai, and half a book of notes that he had written densely. He sat down and began to outline his speech.
On the first page, he wrote the title of the report: "Observation and Speculation on the Basics of Medical Medicine for Mortals".
